elements.label: Figure O.8: Change in number of wage jobs, 2010–2020
elements.description: Grouped bar chart. Y-axis: 'Net change in employment (millions)', ranging from -3 to 5 in steps of 1. X-axis categories: 2010–14 and 2015–20. Legend: Wage worker (teal), Employer (orange), Own account worker (grey), Unpaid family worker (yellow). Approximate readings: 2010–14: Wage worker ~2.2, Employer ~-0.6, Own account worker ~0.3, Unpaid family worker ~1.8. 2015–20: Wage worker ~4.9, Employer ~-0.1, Own account worker ~-1.9, Unpaid family worker ~-2.4. No values are printed on the chart. Source: GSO, Labor Force Survey. The pattern shows strong wage-job gains in 2010–14 and 2015–20, with the 2015–20 wage-worker gain largest, while own-account and unpaid family workers declined in the later period.

elements.label: Figure O.9: Number of jobs by skill level, 2010–2020
elements.description: Grouped bar chart. Y-axis: 'Net change in employment (millions)', ranging from -4 to 4 in steps of 1. X-axis categories: 2010–14 and 2015–20. Legend: High-skill (teal), Medium-skill (orange), Low-skill (grey). Approximate readings: 2010–14: High-skill ~0.75, Medium-skill ~1.0, Low-skill ~2.05. 2015–20: High-skill ~0.8, Medium-skill ~2.85, Low-skill ~-3.1. No values are printed on the chart. Source: GSO, Labor Force Survey. The pattern shows all skill groups gaining jobs in 2010–14, while in 2015–20 medium-skill jobs grew most strongly and low-skill jobs declined sharply.
